To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
smooth pursuit is enhanced for the visual target that is selected by a saccade and that this target-selective enhancement occurs after the saccade, not before.

smooth pursuit eye velocity is spatially selective after a saccade that lands near one of the two visual targets, that the saccade must occur to trigger target selection in pursuit, and that the latency of saccades determines whether the pursuit before the saccade reflects a vector average of responses to the two targets or is spatially selective.
saccades with long latencies (i.e., >200 msec) are almost always targeting s accades, and that pursuit enhancement is spatially selective for targets and time-locked to saccades.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms that allow us to see, hear and move.
the mechanisms that control the direction of saccades and smooth eye movements, and with how the motor commands for these movements are coordinated.
how the brain selects the appropriate motor action when multiple targets and distractors are present in the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the smooth pursuit system is a target-selective system, and that the selection process can be initiated by a saccadic eye movement.
the motor commands of the saccades play an important role in the enhancement of the pursuit and in the target selection for the pursuit.

the saccades and the post-saccadic pursuit eye movements in the present experiments were both target-selective, but that the saccade target-selection process occurred earlier in time than the post-saccade target-selection for pursuit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
smooth eye movements are not only controlled by a motor program for the eye movement, but also by the motor program for saccades.
the visual-motor system uses saccadic eye movements to choose a single target for smooth pursuit.
the motor commands of the saccadic system are involved in selecting the target for smooth pursuit eye movements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
saccades and smooth pursuit can work together to enhance the transmission of visual motion signals, and this enhancement is spatially selective.
saccades and smooth pursuit are tightly coupled and may share a common mechanism for target selection.
the selection of a target for smooth pursuit eye movements is spatially selective for a saccade target.
